_leia: PROSE LAYER — translation. Facts live in nucleo.json. The _hash field records the Portuguese source at the moment of translation.

maeda.corpo: A Kodokan apprentice from 1897, he left on a diffusion mission in 1904 with stops across the United States, Europe, Mexico, Cuba and Central America. He landed in Pará and settled in Belém until his death. He travelled often for exhibitions, leaving classes to his graded students.
maeda.nota: He promoted five Brazilians to the first stripe — the only promotion of Brazilians by him that can be confirmed. Carlos Gracie is not on the list.

ferro.corpo: Maeda's leading Brazilian student and instructor at the Belém academy whenever the master travelled. Teacher of Donato Pires dos Reis and Carlos Gracie.
ferro.nota: Were it not for a handful of period newspaper articles, he would have vanished from the record entirely. He is the link the enshrined narrative erases.

franca.corpo: Founder of the principal non-Gracie lineage. He taught military personnel and residents of Rio's North Zone communities, emphasising self-defence and charging most students nothing.
franca.nota: His role as a forerunner of the Marine Corps self-defence system was never recorded by the Navy's sporting administration — it survived as oral account from former students. That is the most economical explanation for the documentary vacuum.
franca.lacuna: Birthplace disputed. Civil registry not located.
